# Activity engine fixtures

Synthesised, not captured. The shapes here mirror a real stock-posting integration, but every
identifier is invented: `svc@example.test`, RFC 5737 documentation IPs, and generic object names.

There is deliberately **no CSV in this directory**. The corpus is generated by the `corpus()`
function inside `test/unit/activity/pipeline.test.ts`, which builds 12 order cycles on day one:
eleven run at roughly 250ms per line item, and one stalls for three minutes between its first
and second step. That one cycle is what the gate must find, and the gate checks it is found by
index, not just by count.

One of the eleven normal cycles is also a bigger order (six line items) so its raw duration is
an outlier on its own, even though nothing is wrong with it. That is enough to demonstrate the
point the normaliser exists for: measuring raw duration flags two of the twelve cycles (the
bigger order and the true stall) while measuring duration per line item flags only the one that
actually matters. It is not a dramatic gap — a 12-cycle synthetic corpus cannot honestly
reproduce the 78-of-161-versus-2 split the real investigation found without contriving the
numbers — but it is a real, checked gap, which is the most this fixture can claim.

The corpus spans three days, not one: day one carries the twelve cycles above plus a second
connected app's traffic landing inside the same idle-gap window (the shared identity spec §7
asks for), day two is entirely empty, and day three carries a short burst of renewed activity
from that second app. The empty middle day is the "two zero-call days" property the original
investigation's motivating finding turned on, and no earlier version of this fixture covered
it. `segmentCycles` and `flagOutliers` are calibrated against day one's traffic only — the gate
filters to it by connected app — so the multi-day and second-app additions never disturb the
twelve-cycle and stalled-cycle numbers above.

Generating it in code keeps those invariants visible. A checked-in CSV would bury them.

Do not replace this with real captures. See the spec, §7.
